semantics: arg0 outside the Ship table -> 0; the type's wareListIndex <= 0 -> 0. Else Trade::CountWareInWareList(wares, list, subtype=(int16)arg2, class=(int16)arg1): number of entries of the ware list equal to that ware type key. Sync.

name: SA_GetWareListWareCount
summary: Returns how many of a ware a predefined ware list contains.
semantics: list <= 0 -> 0. Else Trade::CountWareInWareList(ware lists, list, (int16)arg3, (int16)arg2): the amount of ware (class arg2, subtype arg3) in ware list number list (the lists ships use for predefined cargo, cf. SA_GetShipTypePredefinedWareCount). No upper bound check on list in the handler. Answers at once.
notes: AP case jumps into SA_GetShipTypePredefinedWareCount's tail (0x00464e66). Upper bound of list not checked here (inside the helper not read).

name: SA_GetTypeShieldPowerGeneration
summary: Returns the shield power generation of a ship, factory or dock type.
semantics: Invalid type -> 0. Ship -> ShipType.energyBudget (the ship's shield generator power); Factory -> factory row shieldPower; Dock -> dock row shieldPower; any other class -> 0. Answers at once.

name: SA_GetTypeNumDockPorts
summary: Returns the number of dock ports of a station/dock/ship type.
semantics: Invalid type -> 0. Else Dock::GetTypeNumDockPorts(subtype, class): the port count of the type's port set (carriers' and stations' docking ports); types without ports -> 0. Answers at once.
notes: FL calls an unnamed copy (FUN_00444100); not compared instruction by instruction.

name: SA_GetTypeDockBaySize
summary: Returns how many ships a ship type's hangar holds.
semantics: Invalid type -> 0. Ship class -> ShipType dock bay size (TShips 'docking slots' field at row+0xac); any other class -> 0. Answers at once.
notes: FL inlines Ship::GetTypeDockBaySize: class 7 -> shipRows[sub]+0xac, else 0 (FL 0x0046f93f).

name: SA_GetTypeIsDockingPossibleOf
summary: Tells whether ships of a given ship type can dock at a type (class, subtype).
semantics: Invalid (class, subtype) -> 0. Else Dock::TypeIsDockingPossibleOf(class, subtype, arg3): arg3 is the docking ship's type (ship subtype / class code as the port set expects); 1 if any port of the target type accepts it. Answers at once.
notes: FL calls an unnamed copy (FUN_00444160); arg3 meaning not verified in the helper.

name: SA_GetTypeCanUseDockPort
summary: Tells whether a given ship type may use a given dock port of a type.
semantics: Invalid (class, subtype) -> 0. Else Dock::TypeCanUseDockPort(class, subtype, shiptype = arg4, port = arg3, flag = arg5 payload non-zero). Note the argument order to the helper: arg4 before arg3. Answers at once.
notes: Meaning of the boolean arg5 not verified.

name: SA_GetTypeDockPortAnimFlags
summary: Returns the door animation flags of a dock port of a type.
semantics: Invalid type -> 0. Else Dock::GetTypeDockPortAnimFlags(subtype, port = arg3, class). Used with SA_StartDockPortAnim. Answers at once.

name: SA_GetTypeDockPortFlags
summary: Returns the dock port flags of a type.
semantics: Invalid type -> 0. Else Dock::GetTypeDockPortFlags(subtype, class) (per-type port set flags). Answers at once.

name: SA_GetShipTypeNumCockpits
summary: Returns the number of cockpits (view points) of a ship type.
semantics: arg0 outside the Ship table -> 0, else shipRows[arg0].viewPointCount. Sync.

name: SA_GetShipTypeNumTurrets
summary: Returns the number of gun groups (turrets incl. the main guns) of a ship type.
semantics: arg0 outside the Ship table -> 0, else shipRows[arg0].gunGroupCount. Sync.

name: SA_GetShipTypeNumLasersInTurret
returns: int: number of laser (gun) slots in the gun group
summary: Returns the number of laser slots of a gun group (turret) of a ship type.
semantics: arg0 outside the Ship table -> 0; turret outside 0..gunGroupCount-1 -> 0; else gunGroups[turret].gunSlotCount. Sync.

name: SA_GetShipTypeNumGunsInTurret
returns: int: number of slots in the gun group
summary: Returns the number of slots of a gun group (turret) of a ship type.
semantics: arg0 outside the Ship table -> 0; turret outside 0..gunGroupCount-1 -> 0; else gunGroups[turret].slotCount. Sync.
notes: slotCount vs gunSlotCount (SA_GetShipTypeNumLasersInTurret) are two different columns of the gun group record.

name: SA_GetMaxShipTypeLasers
summary: Returns the total number of laser (gun) slots of a ship type.
semantics: arg0 outside 0..count(Ship)-1 -> 0, else shipRows[arg0].gunCount. Sync.

name: SA_SetBgTypeData
args: index:int, family:string, nstars:int, nnebulae:int, noutside:int, dust:array[8], ndust:int, ambient:int(0xRRGGBB), hue:int, fognear:int, fogfar:int, stardust:int, dustcolour:int(0xRRGGBB)
summary: Defines or edits a background type (stars, nebulae, dust, colours, fog) at runtime.
semantics: count = number of Background types. index == count appends a row (id string 'SS_BG_<index+1>'); 0 <= index < count edits that row. Fields: familyName = arg2 if a string; star/nebula/outside body counts = arg3..arg5; dustWeight[0..7] = arg6[0..7]; numDust = arg7; ambient colour = arg8 split into R,G,B bytes; hue = arg9; fogNear/fogFar = arg10/arg11; stardustPercent = arg12; dust colour = arg13 split. Bodies are then registered by name: 'environments\nebulae\<family>\nebula_<family>' + '_stars_NN' (NN = 01..nstars), '_background_NN' (nnebulae), '_outside_partNN' (noutside), '_dust_partNN' (always 8); unused slots set to 0. Answers 0 (after the table edit). Used by background editor scripts; sectors pick the change up at SA_ResetSectorBackground.
x3_src: differs: B117 (index outside 0..count, or body counts above 16/16/8, change nothing and answer 0) and B124 (arg6 must be an array of >= 8)
bugs: AP 0x00467ac3: for index outside 0..count the table grows by one row but row index is written (about 0xdb8 bytes per step out of bounds); counts arg3..arg5 bound the loops writing starBodies[16], nebulaBodies[16], outsideBodies[8] without limit (heap corruption); arg6 elements dereferenced unchecked. Fixed in x3_src (B117, B124).

name: SA_BgTypeFromBody
returns: int: 1 star body, 2 nebula body, 0 neither
summary: Tells whether a body id is used as a background star body (1) or nebula body (2) by any background type.
semantics: Object::BgTypeFromBody: walks all background types (class Background rows, TBackgrounds); for each row first its starBodies[0..starBodyCount) then nebulaBodies[0..nebulaBodyCount); the first match returns 1 (star) or 2 (nebula); no match or no rows -> 0. Pure lookup, no side effects. Sync.

name: SA_StopObject
summary: Stops a ship's current flight order and wakes the task waiting on the object with a result.
semantics: obj missing -> 0. Non-ship: only Script::WakeTaskWithResult(obj, arg2): if a task waits on this object (an earlier waiting SA_ movement native stored its group slot and task id in the object), its native group's int-done callback resumes that task with arg2; the link is cleared. Ship: if the order is PlayerLanding: requestedPortIndex = -1 and the script method NotifyDockingAbort(obj id) of the SA module object is called; if the order is WarpIn: the subtree override effect is cleared, the node is put at the order point and flag ScriptWarpEffect is cleared. Then order = Stopped, nextThinkTime = game time, flag StoredInContainer cleared, and WakeTaskWithResult(obj, arg2). The calling task is answered 0 at once; the woken task (usually another one, blocked in SA_MovePos, SA_TurnToObject etc.) gets arg2 as that native's result.

name: SA_ForceMove

notes: FL uses FUN_004c59b0 in place of Script::CellIsTrue (same role).

name: SA_FireOnObject

summary: Fires a ship's guns of one gun group at a target object.
semantics: ship by id (missing -> 0); arg1 non-zero -> target by id (may be missing -> NULL, then the cockpit's tracked object is used). mask = arg4 if argc >= 5 else -1. Ship::FireControl(ship, target, group=arg2, flags=arg3, mask): see SA_FireAhead for the rules; with a target and flag 1 the guns aim at it. Sync.

name: SA_FireAhead
returns: int: 0xb no shot fired, 0xc shot fired (Ship::FireControl result); 0 if the ship is missing
summary: Fires a ship's guns of one gun group straight ahead (no target).
semantics: ship by id (missing -> 0). Ship::FireControl(ship, target=NULL, group=arg2, flags=arg3, mask): group < 0 or >= the ship type's gun-group count, no root node, not in a sector, or docked -> 0xb. With no target the active cockpit's tracked object of that group is used if any. Each active laser in the group whose slot bit (slot - first slot of group) is set in mask fires if reloaded and has energy (tractor beam only for the player with flag 2). Flags: 1 aim at target, 2 player shot, 4 ignore facing cone, 8 skip ship motion, 0x20 cursor aim. Original: mask = arg4 when argc >= 4, else -1 (all guns). arg1 is not read. Sync.
x3_src: differs: B135 (mask read only when argc >= 5; with 4 arguments the mask is -1)
bugs: AP 0x00461b3f (B135): CMP argc,4 then reads arguments[4]: with exactly 4 arguments the gun mask is the stale cell after the last argument. Fixed in x3_src. Not called by stock scripts.

name: SA_ShootMissileOnObject

semantics: ship = FindByIdInWorld(arg1) (missing -> 0); target = FindByIdInWorld(arg2) (may be NULL). Ship::LaunchMissile(ship, target, 0, arg3, arg4 if argc >= 4 else 0, arg5 if argc >= 5 else 0): the type argument is 0, arg3 takes the 'a' position of SA_ShootMissile (in x3_src the same parameter that SA_ShootMissile passes arg4 to). Answer = missile id or 0. Answers at once.
x3_src: differs: B130 - an invalid missile type launches nothing (answer 0)
bugs: Same unchecked type read as SA_ShootMissile (B130), fixed in x3_src.
notes: Which LaunchMissile parameter selects the missile type here (arg3?) not verified; LaunchMissile not read.

name: SA_ShootMissile
args: ship:id, missiletype:int, target:id, a:int | ... , b:int | ..., b:int, c:int
summary: Launches a missile of a given type from a ship (optionally at a target).
semantics: ship = FindByIdInWorld(arg1) (missing -> 0); target = Object::FindById(arg3) (global lookup, any world; may be NULL). Ship::LaunchMissile(ship, target, type = arg2, arg4, arg5 if argc >= 5 else 0, arg6 if argc >= 6 else 0) creates the missile object in the ship's sector; answer = the new missile's id, or 0 if nothing was launched. Does not consume a missile from the ship's cargo here (unless LaunchMissile does). Answers at once.
x3_src: differs: B130 - a missile type outside the TMissiles table launches nothing (answer 0)
bugs: AP 0x00461d9c -> Object::LaunchMissile 0x00448b30 reads missileRows()[(int16)type].flags without a range check: wrong flags/speed/lifetime or a crash for a bad type. Fixed in x3_src (B130).

name: SA_FindNearestEnemy

semantics: Sector found -> stores arg2 into the second background body index field (read back by SA_GetSectorBackgroundNebulasIndex, used by the next SA_ResetSectorBackground), answer arg2; missing -> 0. No range check here.

name: SA_GetSectorBackgroundNebulasIndex
returns: int: the sector's background nebula body index
summary: Returns which nebula body of its background type a sector uses.
semantics: Sector::FindById(arg0); not a sector -> 0. Returns Sector +0x144 (the value written by SA_SetSectorBackgroundNebulasIndex, case 0x137). Use with SA_GetBgTypeNebulaBodyID(bgType, index). Sync.
notes: x3_src names the +0x144 field 'starsBodyIndex' and +0x140 'nebulaBodyIndex' (swapped relative to these natives' names); behaviour is identical (same offsets as AP). Naming only.

name: SA_GetTimer
summary: Returns the script timer base value (only for timer 0).
semantics: arg1 payload non-zero -> 0. arg1 == 0 -> EngineConfig.scriptTimerZero (the game-time base word kept for scripts). Answers at once.
notes: What scriptTimerZero counts (ms of game time) not re-verified.

name: SA_AllocTextInst
returns: int: scene node handle, 0 on failure
summary: Creates a 3D text node (one glyph child per character) and returns its node handle.
semantics: arg0 via CellGetString (non-string -> NULL text), arg1 = flags passed to Scene::CreateText3DNode. The node is created hidden (not attached to any scene); the script attaches/positions it with B3D_ natives and frees it with the B3D node free native. Returns node->handle, or 0 if creation failed. Sync.

name: SA_FreeAllBodies
summary: Purges all loaded 3D bodies and reloads the bodies of the current scenes (memory clean-up).
semantics: Scene::DisableAllObjects3D; Mesh::PurgeAllBodies(0) frees every loaded body/mesh; Scene::ReloadSceneBodies reloads the bodies still used by scenes; Object::RebuildAllCollisionTrees; then ticks the game clock wrapper (so the long load is not counted as game time). Heavy: causes a hitch. Sync.

name: SA_CleanUpObjects
summary: Destroys every object that was allocated but never placed anywhere (no parent), except sectors.
semantics: Object::CleanUpUnplaced: walks the world's object list; every object of class != Space with parent == NULL gets the Destroyed flag and NotifyRemoved(0) (references to it are cleared; it is freed by the normal destroyed-object sweep). Ids of such objects (from SA_AllocObject not yet started) become invalid. Sync.

name: SA_ObjectTypeFromBody
summary: Finds the type whose body id is the given body and returns class<<16|subtype.
semantics: Object::FindTypeByTypeId(arg1, &class, &index): scans the type tables (all classes) for the first row whose bodyId equals arg1; found -> ((int16)class<<16)|index, else 0. Answers at once.
notes: Search order (class order, first match) as described for findTypeByTypeId in bugs.md B114.

name: SA_ObjectTypeFromCut
summary: Finds the type whose cut id is the given value and returns class<<16|subtype.
semantics: Object::FindTypeByValueInObjectCategories(arg1, &class, &index): first type (in class order) whose cut/scene id equals arg1; found -> (class<<16)|index, else 0. Answers at once.

name: SA_IsSpecialBody
summary: Tells whether a body id is in one of the special body lists (or a given one).
semantics: Object::IsSpecialBody(body = arg1, list = arg2): 1 if any of the counted special body lists (list index == arg2, or all when arg2 == -1) contains the body, else 0. Answers at once.

name: SA_IsDummyBody
summary: Tells whether a body id is a dummy (helper) body, optionally in one dummy table.
semantics: Scene dummy tables: answer 1 if body arg1 occurs in dummy table arg2 (or in any table when arg2 == -1), else 0. Answers at once.

name: SA_CreateObjectCutScene
returns: int: scene node handle, 0 on failure
summary: Builds the scene (node tree) of a type/body id under an optional parent node and returns its node handle.
semantics: arg0 = body/type id; arg1 non-zero -> parent = Scene::NodeFromHandle(arg1) else none; arg3 non-zero -> owner object by id else none; arg2 is read as a string but ignored. World::BuildSceneFromType(bodyId, parent, owner, 0) loads the body/cut and builds its nodes; result = root node handle, 0 if nothing was built. The nodes belong to the parent (or are free-standing; the caller frees them with B3D natives). Sync.

name: SA_SetDesiredDistance
summary: Sets a follow camera's distance (offset) from its target.
semantics: Object found and class Camera -> CameraFollowData.offset = arg2 (length units); other classes/missing: nothing. Read back by SA_GetDesiredDistance. Answers 0.

name: SA_GetDesiredDistance
summary: Returns a camera object's desired follow distance.
semantics: object by id, must be class Camera else 0. Returns CameraFollowData.offset (the follow distance set by SA_SetDesiredDistance). Sync.

name: SA_SetDestination
summary: Sets the target object of a ship order, a missile or a follow camera.
semantics: dest = FindByIdInWorld(arg2) if arg2's payload is non-zero, else NULL (clears). obj found -> by class: Ship -> ShipData.orderTarget = dest; Missile -> MissileData.target = dest; Camera -> CameraFollowData.target = dest; other classes: nothing. A non-existent dest id stores NULL. SA_GetDestination reads it. The stored pointer is a raw object pointer the engine clears when the target dies. Answers 0.

name: SA_IsWarpOutSlotAvailable
summary: Tells whether a jump gate has a free exit slot for an arriving ship.
semantics: Object found and class Warpgate -> looks at the gate's 6 exit slots (GateData): 1 as soon as a slot has no object or its expiry time minus current game time <= 0; all 6 busy -> 0. Non-gate or missing -> 0. Read-only (does not reserve the slot). Answers at once.

name: SA_SetCameraConnectMode
summary: Sets how a follow camera is connected to its target (axis/mode).
semantics: Object found and class Camera -> CameraFollowData.axis = arg2 (the camera follow mode/axis selector used by the camera update). Otherwise nothing. Answers 0.
notes: Mode values not enumerated.

name: SA_SetCameraB3DCamera
summary: Binds a B3D camera node to a follow-camera object.
semantics: Object found and class Camera -> CameraFollowData.extra = Scene::FindEnabledNodeById(arg2) (the B3D camera node; NULL if the handle is unknown, which unbinds). The camera object then drives that B3D camera. Otherwise nothing. Answers 0.

name: SA_SetSpeedLimit
summary: Sets a ship's speed limit field.
semantics: Object found and class Ship -> ShipData.speedLimit = arg2 (raw speed units; the motion code caps speed by it, 0 presumably = no limit). Non-ship/missing: nothing. Answers 0.
notes: Consumer semantics (0 = none) not verified.

name: SA_SetMaxSpeedOverride
summary: Sets a ship's max speed override.
semantics: Object found and class Ship -> ShipData.speedOverride = arg2 (raw speed units; used in place of the computed max speed by the speed code when non-zero). Non-ship/missing: nothing. Answers 0.
notes: Consumer semantics not verified.

name: SA_SetMaxStrafeSpeedOverride
summary: Sets a ship's max strafe speed override.
semantics: Object found and class Ship -> ShipData.maxStrafeSpeedOverride = arg2. Non-ship/missing: nothing. Answers 0.

name: SA_SetPosAndDirection
summary: Sets position and facing direction of an object from a 9-element array.
semantics: obj found -> SetPosition(arr[0], arr[1], arr[2]) as SA_SetPos, then SetOrientationFromDirection with the direction (arr[6], arr[7], arr[8]) as SA_SetDirection; arr[3..5] (the Euler angles in SA_GetPosRotAndDirection's layout) are ignored. The array is read with ArrayGetElement; elements are raw dwords. Missing object: nothing. Answers 0.
x3_src: differs: B129 - a non-array or an array shorter than 9 is ignored (answer 0)
bugs: AP 0x00465db6: ArrayGetElement(i)->value read without NULL test - a non-array argument or fewer than 9 elements crashes (read at address 1). Fixed in x3_src (B129).

name: SA_SetSafePosAndDirection
summary: Places an object at a free spot near a position (array) and sets its facing direction.
semantics: obj found -> Ship::FindFreeArrivalOffset(obj, arr[0], arr[1], arr[2]) (as SA_SetSafePos with 4 arguments: the exact position if free, else up to 20 random tries around it), then SetOrientationFromDirection(arr[6], arr[7], arr[8]); arr[3..5] ignored. Answers 0.
x3_src: differs: B126 (no scene node -> ignored) and B129 (non-array or < 9 elements -> ignored)
bugs: AP 0x00465e46: array elements dereferenced unchecked (B129) and rootNode unchecked (B126): crash for a short/non-array argument or a sector id. Fixed in x3_src.

name: SA_GetPosRotAndDirection
returns: int: always 0 (results written into the array argument)
summary: Writes an object's position, rotation angles and forward direction into a caller-supplied array.
semantics: As SA_GetPosAndRot plus [6..8] = root node rotation row 2 (forward axis x,y,z, fixed-point ratio). Writes into the existing array arg1 in place. Missing object: nothing written. Original: no root node check, so a sector id crashes. Always answers 0. Sync.
x3_src: differs: B126 (object without root node writes nothing)
bugs: AP 0x00465ed6 (B126): sector id dereferences NULL root node; fixed in x3_src.

name: SA_SetPosAndRot
summary: Sets position and Euler angles of an object from a 6-element array.
semantics: obj found -> SetPosition(arr[0], arr[1], arr[2]) then SetAngles(arr[3], arr[4], arr[5]) (alpha, beta, gamma; 1/65536 turn). Layout as SA_GetPosAndRot fills it. Answers 0.
x3_src: differs: B129 - non-array or < 6 elements -> ignored
bugs: AP 0x00465f8b: unchecked ArrayGetElement results - crash for a short/non-array argument. Fixed in x3_src (B129).

name: SA_SetSafePosAndRot
summary: Places an object at a free spot near a position and sets its Euler angles.
semantics: obj found -> Ship::FindFreeArrivalOffset(obj, arr[0], arr[1], arr[2]) then SetAngles(arr[3], arr[4], arr[5]). Answers 0.
x3_src: differs: B126 and B129 - no scene node or a short/non-array argument -> ignored
bugs: AP 0x00466017: unchecked array elements (B129) and rootNode (B126) - crash. Fixed in x3_src.

name: SA_GetPosAndRot
returns: int: always 0 (results written into the array argument)
summary: Writes an object's position and rotation angles into a caller-supplied array.
semantics: object by id; if found and it has a root node, the existing array arg1 gets [0..2] = root node local position x,y,z (sector coordinates, engine units), [3..5] = motion.rotAlpha, rotBeta, rotGamma (script angle units). The array is modified in place (ArraySetInt; elements past its size or a non-array are silently not written). Missing object / no root node: array untouched. Always answers 0. Sync.

name: SA_TransformPosAndRot
summary: Composes two position+angle transforms.
semantics: base and rel are [x, y, z, a, b, c]. Result = new array: position = rel.pos + base.pos * R(rel); rotation = R(base) * R(rel) converted to Euler angles, stored as [3] = c, [4] = a, [5] = b of the conversion (the same order the cut transform natives use). The array is owned by the script. Answers at once.
x3_src: differs: B124 - a non-array or < 6 elements answers int 0
bugs: AP 0x00466124: array elements dereferenced unchecked - crash for a non-array/short array. Fixed in x3_src (B124).

name: SA_GetRelativePos
returns: array[3]: base position + rel rotated by the base angles, or int 0
summary: Transforms a relative offset by a base position and rotation and returns the resulting position.
semantics: A new 3-element array. R = AnglesToMatrix(base[3], base[4], base[5]); result = base[0..2] + rel[0..2] * R (engine units). The task gets the array. Original: elements read via ArrayGetElement without NULL checks, so a non-array or short array crashes. Sync.
x3_src: differs: B124 (base shorter than 6 or rel shorter than 3, or not arrays -> int 0)
bugs: AP (B124): ArrayGetElement NULL not checked: non-array/short array crashes; fixed in x3_src.
notes: FL uses FUN_0050d400 for the angle->matrix step (unnamed in x3fl).

name: SA_GetBulletTypeFlyFX
returns: int: the bullet type's flag word
summary: Returns a bullet type's effect/flag word (fly FX flags).
semantics: arg0 outside the Bullet table -> 0, else bulletRows[arg0].typeFlags (bit 0x40 = needs ammunition; other bits select flight effects). Sync.

name: SA_SetEnemyOfEnabled
summary: Enables or disables the object's 'enemy of' hostility flag.
semantics: obj found -> Relation::SetEnemyOfEnabled(obj, arg2 != 0): for class Ship, Dock or Factory stores the flag at data+0x1d4 (read by the hostility test Relation::IsHostile step 1); other classes nothing. Answers 0.
notes: Stores (arg2 != 0) as 0/1 in AP (SETNZ at 0x00466881) and FL; FL inlines the setter (0x0047117a).

name: SA_GetMissileAim
returns: int: target object id, 0 if none
summary: Returns the target of a missile object.
semantics: object by id; must be class Missile; returns MissileData.target id, 0 if missing/not a missile/no target. Sync.

name: SA_GetNumFactoryConnectionPoints
summary: Returns the number of complex connection points of a factory.
semantics: object by id; missing -> 0. Station::GetNumFactoryConnectionPoints: non-Factory -> 0; else counts the root node's child parts whose body is a connection dummy set (body 0x28cc = 4 connections, 0x291c = 3, others via the dummy set), capped at 32. Sync.
notes: Counting rule per body only partly read.

name: SA_CreateFactoryConnections
returns: array: one element per station, each array [parentStationId, stationId, tubePartId...]; int 0 on failure
summary: Builds the connecting tubes of a factory complex (hub + stations) and returns the created tube part ids per station.
semantics: hub (arg0) by id; missing -> int 0. Script::SaCreateFactoryConnections(hub, world, arg1, &result): result starts as int 0; stationCount = size of the arg1 array (non-array -> 0). A temporary table of stationCount+1 records (entry 0 = the hub) is allocated (freed again before return). collectFactoryConnectionPoints reads every station's connection dummy nodes (position, rotation, direction; fails -> result stays 0). linkFactoryStations then links each station to the nearest free connection point of an already linked station (greedy nearest pair, a spanning tree from the hub). spawnFactoryConnectors creates, per link, two end pieces (type keys 0x14002d at the parent's point, 0x14002f at the station's point; class 20 Special) and enough tube segments (0x14002e) scaled along z to span the gap; all are added to the hub's sector (parent) and become ordinary world objects owned by the sector (the script must free them itself when dismantling the complex). Result: a new array of stationCount elements, element r-1 = [id of the linked parent station (or hub), station id, ids of the parts created for this link...]. The task gets it via ResumeTaskWithCell; the dispatcher then releases its own reference. Sync.
notes: Helper read in x3_src (object_script.cpp:456), not in the exe; collectFactoryConnectionPoints' acceptance rules (which nodes count as connection points, failure cases) only skimmed.

name: SA_DecoupleShips
returns: int: 0 at once, or (when waiting) the completion result
summary: Plays a decoupling cut scene that spawns/animates the ships or objects it describes; waits while a given ship animates.
semantics: arg0 non-zero -> ship by id (else none). Ship::DecoupleShips(cutId=arg2, ship, arg1, arg3): a ship given must be class Ship with a root node and a script object, else returns 0; loads the cut (Scene::LoadCutScene; fail -> 0), replaces the ship's root by the cut, announces mode-1 parts as objects/ships (script events with arg1/arg2), and animates them. If no ship was given -> answers 0 at once. If a ship was given and DecoupleShips returned non-zero, the task waits on that ship (scriptLink) until the decoupling animation ends (WakeTaskWithResult); else answers 0. Used by carrier/ship-launch cut scenes.
notes: Ship::DecoupleShips body only skimmed; exact completion value and event contents not verified.

name: SA_StartInGameScene
summary: Starts an in-game cut scene bound to an object.
semantics: obj found -> answer = Script::StartInGameScene(world, obj, arg2, arg3, arg4) (the in-game scene system: camera/cut playback around the object; the arguments are the scene/cut id and its parameters as the KC InGameScene class passes them). Missing object -> 0. Answers at once; the scene runs on its own afterwards (scripts poll or wait on it separately).
notes: Script::StartInGameScene not read; argument meaning unverified.

name: SA_StartInGameScene2
summary: Starts an in-game scene without a bound object (second form).
semantics: Answer = Script::StartInGameScene2(world, arg1, arg2). Answers at once.
notes: StartInGameScene2 not read; arguments unknown.

name: SA_ReloadShipLasers
summary: Refills a ship's laser energy to its type maximum.
semantics: Object found and class Ship -> ShipData.laserEnergy = TShips[subtype].maxLaserEnergy * 1000 (the type's maximum, not the installed-generator maximum Object::GetMaxLaserEnergy). Otherwise nothing. Answers 0.

name: SA_SetShipAtDockPort
summary: Attaches a ship to (or frees) a given dock port of a station/carrier.
semantics: container missing -> 0. ship = FindByIdInWorld(arg3) if non-zero, else NULL (release the port). Answer = Dock::AttachShipToPort(container, port = arg2, ship, arg4) (positions the ship on the port and records it in the port record; returns non-zero on success). Answers at once.
notes: AttachShipToPort not read: meaning of arg4 and the return value unknown; no port range check seen in the handler (check is inside the helper, if any).

name: SA_StartDockPortAnim
summary: Starts the door animation of a dock port.
semantics: obj found -> Dock::AnimatePortDoors(obj, port = arg2, arg3, (DoorMode)arg4) (open/close the port's door parts; see SA_GetTypeDockPortAnimFlags). Answers 0.
notes: AnimatePortDoors not read; arg3 and DoorMode values unknown.

name: SA_GetDockPortPosInst
returns: int: scene node handle of the port node, 0 if none
summary: Returns the scene node handle of a container's dock port node suitable for a ship type code.
semantics: container by id (missing -> 0). AP: Dock::ChoosePortNodeByTypeCode(port=arg1, container, code=arg2) picks the port's node for that docking class code (-1 = M5/any); NULL -> 0, else node->handle. Sync.
notes: FL 0x004718c7 passes the same arguments (object, arg1, arg2) to 0x0045b9b0, which the x3fl database names Dock::ChoosePortNodeByShipTypeIndex while AP calls Dock::ChoosePortNodeByTypeCode 0x00451df0; probably a name mismatch in the x3fl database (FL body not compared).

name: SA_GetDockPortRendezvousPos
returns: array[3] [x,y,z] of the approach point, or int 0
summary: Returns the rendezvous (approach) point in front of a container's dock port for a ship.
semantics: container (arg0) and ship (arg2) by id; missing -> 0. Dock::GetPortApproachPoint(port=arg1, container, ship, -1, &pos, 0, 0) fails -> 0. Else a new 3-element array of the world position (engine units). Sync.
x3_src: differs: B120 (port and container class bounded in GetPortApproachPoint), B133 (non-Ship ship uses type code -1)
bugs: AP (B120/B133): port index unbounded and DockData assumed for any non-ship container; non-ship subtype indexes shipRows(); fixed in x3_src.

name: SA_FindNearestDockPort
returns: int: the port number (from the list) nearest to the ship, -1 if none
summary: From a list of dock port numbers, returns the one whose port node is nearest the ship (ports in the player's view count closer).
semantics: container (arg0) and ship (arg2) by id; arg1 must be an array of port numbers. Missing object or non-array -> -1. For each port p in the list: node = Dock::ChoosePortNodeByShipTypeIndex(p, container, ship subtype) (the port node usable by this ship type); if a node is found, d = distance(node world pos, ship pos); if the ship is the player ship and the active control cockpit has a sector camera, a port whose direction from the camera is within cos >= 0.8 of the view axis gets d/10. The port with the smallest d wins. Sync.
x3_src: differs: B133 (a non-Ship 'ship' uses type code -1 (M5) via ChoosePortNodeByTypeCode instead of indexing shipRows() by its subtype)
bugs: AP (B133): the ship's subtype indexes shipRows() for any class (wrong slot or read past the table for non-ships); fixed in x3_src. FL 0x00471ab5 has the same unchecked g_pShipTypeTable[ship subtype] read.
notes: FL 0x004719d0 gets the view via Camera::GetCockpitSceneCamera(registry, activeControlCockpit)+0x58 (= FindByHandle()->sectorCamera) and inlines the port record lookup (port bounded by the container's port count for classes 5/6/7, else NULL record) before choosing the node; equivalent.

name: SA_FindNearestDockPortRendezvous
returns: int: the port number whose rendezvous (approach) point is nearest the ship, -1 if none
summary: From a list of dock port numbers, returns the one whose approach (rendezvous) point is nearest the ship.
semantics: container (arg0), ship (arg2) by id, arg1 array of port numbers; missing/non-array -> -1. For each port: Dock::GetPortApproachPoint(port, container, ship, -1, &pos, 0, 0); if it succeeds, d = distance(pos, ship pos) (AP Math::Distance3); smallest wins. No view weighting. Sync.
x3_src: differs: B133 (non-Ship ship uses type code -1), B120 (port bounds checked in GetPortApproachPoint)
bugs: AP (B120/B133): port index unbounded in GetPortApproachPoint, non-ship subtype indexes shipRows(); fixed in x3_src.
notes: FL computes the distance with Math::SqrtF inline; same result expected.

name: SA_SetShipDockPortNr
summary: Sets the dock port number a ship requests.
semantics: Object found and class Ship -> ShipData.requestedPortIndex = arg2 (-1 = any/none). Otherwise nothing. Answers 0.

name: SA_RestartObjectCut
summary: Ends and restarts the object's cut (part) animations.
semantics: obj found -> Object::EndCutInstances (if obj.sceneId != 0: ends every cut instance on the root node's children, recursively) then Object::RestartCutInstancesIfNear: only if sceneId != 0, the parent is a Space (sector) whose spaceScene exists, and either flags2 CueForcedVisible is set or the view distance is > 0 and < 64 object radii: restarts the ended cut instances on all child nodes. So far-away objects stay stopped until they come near. Answers 0.

name: SA_ShowDummyExplosion
summary: Shows the object's destruction explosion and sound without destroying it.
semantics: obj found and its node is in a scene -> effect = the type's destroyEffect (Ship: TShips row; Factory/Dock: station row; Missile: only when launched, TMissiles row), 0x30 if that is 0 or for other classes; Effect::SpawnLinkedEffect(id, kind 1, effect, obj); if the object is in the active sector, the destroyed sound plays. The object stays alive. Answers 0.
x3_src: differs: B126 - an object without a scene node is ignored
bugs: AP 0x0046408c: rootNode not tested - a sector id crashes. Fixed in x3_src (B126).
notes: sync_scan reports 'may wait' for this case (its path leaves through a shared tail the scan does not follow); the handler answers 0 on every path in x3_src.

name: SA_DeleteAllEffects
summary: Removes all timed effect instances from a sector's space scene and background scene.
semantics: Sector::FindById(arg0); not found -> 0. Effect::ReleaseInstancesForObject on the sector's space scene (if any) and on its background scene (if any): all running timed effect nodes (explosions, particles) of those scenes are released. Sync.

name: SA_SetClientDataFlags
summary: Sets the world's universe/client data flag word.
semantics: World.universeFlags = arg1 (whole word); read back by SA_GetClientDataFlags. Answers 0.

name: SA_GetClientDataFlags
returns: int: the world's universe/client data flag word
summary: Returns the world's universe (client data) flag word.
semantics: Returns World.universeFlags (the flag word written by its setter native, SA_SetClientDataFlags; saved with the universe). No arguments. Sync.
notes: Meaning of the individual bits not decoded here.

name: SA_SaveBackgroundTypes
summary: Writes the background type table (as modified by SA_SetBgTypeData) to a file.
semantics: Script::SaveBackgroundTypes() (debug/editor function: dumps TBackgrounds). Answers 0.
notes: Output file and format not read.

name: SA_StartVideo
summary: Starts a video from the Videos table and returns its table index.
semantics: Media::StartVideo(arg1, owner = arg2): finds the Videos row with id arg1; not found -> -1; else plays its movie (start/end times from the row) bound to owner and returns the row index (pass it to SA_StopVideo). Answers at once.

name: SA_StopVideo
summary: Stops a video started with SA_StartVideo.
semantics: Media::StopVideo(index = arg1, owner = arg2): takes the movie id of Videos[index] (+0x14 of the 0x30-byte row) and stops that movie if it is playing for owner. Answers 0.
bugs: bugs.md B7 (open): the index is not range checked - passing -1 (SA_StartVideo's not-found answer) reads before the Videos table. Same in FL (inlined at 0x00472e29). x3_src reproduces it (g_videoCatalogue.row(index) unchecked).

name: SA_PauseVideo
summary: Pauses or resumes all videos playing on objects in sectors.
semantics: Sector::SetVideosPaused(arg1) (global: all sector video screens/cues). Answers 0.

name: SA_FindVideo
returns: array[7] [movieId, startMin, startSec, startMs, endMin, endSec, endMs], or int 0 if not found
summary: Looks up a video clip record and returns its movie id and start/end times.
semantics: A new 7-element array is created first. Media::FindVideoRecord(arg0): if not found the task is resumed with int 0 (the array is released). Found: elements 0..6 = movie id, start minutes, seconds, milliseconds, end minutes, seconds, milliseconds; the task gets the array (new reference). Sync.

name: SA_GetSpawnInst
summary: Returns the handle of the object's spawn-point child node (body 0x4a56).
semantics: obj found and has a root node -> walks the root node's direct children and returns the handle of the first one whose bodyId == 0x4a56 (19030, the spawn/launch marker body); none, no node or missing object -> 0. Answers at once.

name: SA_TractorConnect
summary: Connects a tractor beam from one ship to another object with an attach offset.
semantics: target = FindByIdInWorld(arg2) if arg2 non-zero. Existing tractor links of the tractor and of the target are released first (Ship::ReleaseTractor on each found object: frees the beam node, clears the old target's tractor flag (its data+0x278 = -1), calls the old target's script method SetTractorTarget(0) unless script-locked, clears both link pointers, recursing to a chain). If both are found: attaches the new beam (Ship::AttachTractorBeam) with the offset (arg3, arg4, arg5). Answers 0.
bugs: unsure: no class test on either object; ReleaseTractor/attach write the target's data+0x278 (a ShipData field) - a non-ship target would get a write beyond its payload (AP 0x004683cd, Ship::ReleaseTractor 0x0044a460). Not verified that the attach path writes it for non-ships; x3_src keeps the same calls.
notes: AttachTractorBeam body not read.

name: SA_TractorDisconnect
summary: Releases any tractor beam the object holds or is held by.
semantics: obj found -> Ship::ReleaseTractor(obj) (see SA_TractorConnect: frees the beam node, resets the target, notifies its script with SetTractorTarget(0), and releases the ship that tractors obj). Answers 0.

name: SA_FindIndexInCut
args: class:int, subtype:int, wantClass:int, wantSubtype:int, frame:array[6], depth:int | ..., start:int | ..., start:int, target:array[3]
returns: int: cut part index, -1 if none
summary: Finds a part of an object type's cut scene whose body is of a wanted class/subtype (random or nearest to a target).
